documents.title: Drafting a generative AI-use policy for your course
documents.summary: A teaching-center guide telling instructors to write a clear AI policy in their syllabus, with a checklist of components, advice on tone and revision, and four sample policies ranging from near-ban to required AI use. It also gives conditions on AI detectors and a list of strategies to reduce unauthorized AI use.
documents.stance_why: The guide sets no campus-wide rule on student AI use; it says "we recommend that you design an generative AI policy that aligns with the specific ethics and practices of your discipline, your department, and your course" and offers four sample policies to adapt, so the decision rests with instructors.

units.why: The guide says "it’s important that you include a clear AI-use policy in your syllabus", addressed to instructors, so it requires a syllabus statement (P09), not a stance.
units.anchor: it’s important that you include a clear AI-use policy in your syllabus

units.why: The sentence "your students won’t know what is expected, what is allowed, and what is prohibited" gives the consequence of omitting a syllabus AI policy, so it explains the instructor duty in the preceding sentence (before-course); it informs rather than directs, and fits P09.
units.anchor: your students won’t know what is expected, what is allowed, and what is prohibited
units.fit_note: A: States the consequence of omitting a syllabus policy rather than the duty itself. B: Gives the reason for having a syllabus policy rather than the requirement itself.
units.resolution_why: Coders split on phase: A course-start, B before-course. The source sentence "If you don’t, your students won’t know what is expected..." is the reason for the preceding duty to put a policy in the syllabus, which both coders placed in before-course. Final: before-course, informs, P09 (both agreed on type and modality).

units.why: "AI detection tools are neither accurate nor reliable" cites Weber-Wulff et al. and says detectors are unreliable, matching P39.

Source: "Multiple studies have found that AI detection tools are neither accurate nor reliable (Weber-Wulff...)", which is an evidence statement, followed by a separate sentence "If they are used, they should be used with caution." Final: this unit is the evidence statement (informs, neutral); the caution rule is kept as its own unit.

units.why: "If they are used, they should be used with caution" allows detectors but advises care; it fits P39 only partly because detectors are not ruled out. I chose P39 over P40 since the emphasis is caution about unreliability.

This is a recommendation distinct from the evidence sentence before it, so it is kept as a separate unit (should, P39 with fit note).

units.policy: At UC Santa Cruz, AI detection software may be used only if it is hosted locally and data is protected from external access, contracted through campus purchasing, or prior written approval is obtained from all students.
